small_guidance:
- The two-pass kernel reads x twice (stats + apply) and recomputes GELU twice. Try a single persistent kernel per (N, group) that loads each element once, accumulates sum/sum² in registers, then re-streams via a second pass over the same group while keeping mean/rstd in registers — eliminates the intermediate mean/rstd global round-trip and one full GELU evaluation if you cache GELU outputs to a scratch buffer (group of 64*65k floats = 16MB, too big — instead recompute GELU but skip the global mean/rstd store/load).
- Autotune stats kernel over BLOCK_SIZE ∈ {2048, 4096, 8192} × num_warps ∈ {8, 16, 32}; the group has 64×258×258 ≈ 4.26M elements so larger BLOCK with more warps may improve bandwidth utilization.
- For the apply kernel, increase BLOCK_SIZE to 4096 or 8192 and drop num_warps to 4 — HW per channel is 258×258=66564, so fewer, fatter programs reduce launch overhead.
large_guidance:
- The ConvTranspose2d almost certainly dominates the 27.5ms runtime (output is 128×64×258×258 ≈ 2.17B elements). Replace it with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: stride=1, kernel=3, so each input element scatters into a 3×3 output neighborhood. With stride=1 this is equivalent to a direct conv of the input (padded) with the flipped kernel — implement as a gather-style im2col GEMM over output tiles where each output pixel reads a 3×3×IC patch from the (zero-padded) input. This is the high-headroom move.
- Fuse bias add + GELU into the conv epilogue (write GELU(conv+bias) directly), then a separate fused GroupNorm pass. Even better: since GroupNorm needs global stats per group, do conv→GELU→write to global, then the existing fused stats+apply kernel — but the conv replacement alone should yield the biggest win.
- Use channels-last layout for the conv output so the GroupNorm reduction along (C_in_group, H, W) has the channel axis contiguous in the inner dimension of the GEMM tile, improving coalescing for both the conv epilogue and the norm pass.
